answer: Agents gain influence only after completing randomly assigned tasks with different peers, who attest to the results; each identity’s attestations are capped. A swarm of new accounts therefore cannot gain weight by appearing alone. The attacker must keep many agents active, perform real work, and build varied interaction histories, while avoiding detectable collusion. A wander across the network may reveal a sable cluster centered on one vertex, but the chief cost is sustained labor and coordination, not creating IDs.
